images.title: Both numbers times the same
images.purpose: Show that 3/8, 6/16 and 9/24 are the same shaded part, and that the top number and the bottom number are both multiplied by 2, or both by 3.
images.composition: Three bars of the same length with the same shaded length: 8 parts with 3 shaded, 16 pieces with 6 shaded, 24 pieces with 9 shaded, their fractions at the right joined by arrows marked ×2 and ×3.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Three bars of the same length stand one above the other, each x 90 to 810 (720 px wide) and 100 px tall, with a 3 px dark #2B2B2B outline; the shaded part of every bar is the first 360 px at the left, filled reddish purple #CC79A7, so the three shaded lengths end at exactly the same place (x 450). BAR 1, y 160 to 260: cut by 7 dark vertical lines (4 px), 90 px apart, into exactly 8 equal parts of 90 px; the first 3 parts are shaded, the other 5 are white. BAR 2, y 360 to 460: the same 7 dark vertical lines as bar 1, and in addition 8 thinner construction grey #6B7280 vertical lines (3 px), one in the middle of each of the 8 parts, so it has exactly 16 equal pieces of 45 px; the first 6 pieces are shaded, the other 10 are white. BAR 3, y 560 to 660: the same 7 dark vertical lines as bar 1, and in addition 16 thinner construction grey #6B7280 vertical lines (3 px), 2 inside each of the 8 parts, so it has exactly 24 equal pieces of 30 px; the first 9 pieces are shaded, the other 15 are white. LABELS, dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (80 px), left aligned at x 860 and centred at y 210, 410 and 610: 3/8 beside bar 1, 6/16 beside bar 2, 9/24 beside bar 3. ARROWS, dark (5 px) with a solid arrowhead: arrow 1 leaves just right of the label 3/8 at (1050, 228), runs right to x 1130, down to y 410 and left to the label 6/16 at x 1055; beside its vertical line, starting at x 1150 and centred at y 310, the text ×2 in dark bold (40 px). Arrow 2 leaves just right of the label 3/8 at (1050, 192), runs right to x 1260, down to y 610 and left to the label 9/24 at x 1055; beside its vertical line, starting at x 1280 and centred at y 400, the text ×3 in dark bold (40 px). The two arrows do not cross. Across the bottom centre at y 740, the line 3/8 = 6/16 = 9/24 in dark bold (64 px). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
shaded lengths that differ between the three bars
a piece count other than 8, 16 and 24, or a shaded count other than 3, 6 and 9
images.takeaway: To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top number and the bottom number by the same number.
images.description: Three bars with the same shaded length named 3/8, 6/16 and 9/24, with arrows from 3/8 marked ×2 to 6/16 and ×3 to 9/24.
images.context: Concept image for The Pattern in Equivalent Fractions. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (copies of one shape with the top and bottom numbers joined by multiplying arrows) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 3/8, 6/16 and 9/24.
images.teaching_notes: Read the arrows as: top ×2 and bottom ×2, then top ×3 and bottom ×3. The slip to watch: adding the same number to the top and the bottom instead of multiplying.

image_decisions.why: The three bars of one shaded length with the ×2 and ×3 arrows show the pattern in the numbers and prove it by the picture.
